page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this instance features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation with no simultaneous multithreading. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 33 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and decompression capabilities. The server achieves a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reads of 294.53 GB/sec and writes of 132.58 GB/sec both rank in the top 25%. Single-threaded and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also place in the top 25%, alongside Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, the ARM64 architecture lacks AVX and AMX instruction sets, and LLM inference for medium 7B models drops to the bottom 25% for prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated ARMv9 core allocation and high memory bandwidth provide high resource density for compute-bound tasks without hyperthreading overhead. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is supported by the 33 Gbps baseline network speed. This hardware profile is suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks, while being less optimal for large language model inference.
